statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The Nasdaq-100 venue is inside the CME weekend halt, and Tail sits well below the block threshold.
recommendation: Mapped policy state remains EA_ON across the whole 24-hour window because every hour falls inside the weekend closure. headline: Weekend halt after a hawkish Warsh Jackson Hole Friday: NQ settled 29,509.50, cash NDX -0.70%, VIX 14.43
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so the entire forecast window is a closed market with no price discovery. Friday's verified evidence: NQ futures settled 29,509.50 (-0.63%) after a 29,437.75-29,811.50 range, cash NDX closed 29,433.43 (-0.70%) near its session low of 29,383.92, and VIX finished at 14.43 with implied volatility contained. Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote struck a hawkish tone on prices and lifted September rate-hike odds from roughly 35% to above even money, with the 10-year yield reported near 4.72% against the H.15 27 August readings of 2Y 4.20% and 10Y 4.67%. WTI near $83.4 and Brent near $88.2 closed a week down roughly 4% on improved Strait of Hormuz flow reporting, which offsets rather than amplifies the hawkish rates impulse. Tail is scored minimal because a halted venue offers no directional efficiency, no retracement behaviour and no extension that mean reversion could fail against. Stress is held low-to-moderate for the unresolved policy repricing and the week-ahead catalyst stack, and stress alone does not lift the mapped policy state. Confidence is high: settlement, cash close, volatility, rates, energy, catalysts and the seven-day calendar are all verified, and the only missing element is a live price path that does not exist during a weekend closure.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span a full Friday session and the start of the weekend halt. Tail ran 11-13 through the Asian and European hours with stress in the high 40s to mid 50s as the market positioned for Jackson Hole. Tail peaked at 22 and stress at 64 in the 16:00-19:00 UTC block, when Warsh's hawkish keynote drove event-driven two-way trade and the mode was scored event/whipsaw, but the mapped policy state never exceeded WATCH because retracements kept occurring. After the 20:00 UTC close the readings decayed quickly - Tail 12 to 6, stress 52 to 24 - as the venue moved into the weekend closure. One hour, 10:00 UTC, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form and Tail is held at 5-6 throughout, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON in all 24 slots. Stress runs 22-26, drifting from low into the moderate band across the second half of the weekend to reflect the unresolved September policy repricing and the 1-4 September catalyst stack of ISM Manufacturing, JOLTS, ADP, jobless claims, ISM Services and August payrolls. Confidence eases from 83 to 78 purely as Friday's verified prints age. The dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify. Weekend headline and gap exposure accumulates but can only be expressed at the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen, which lies beyond this window and belongs to a later assessment with observed evidence.
